howTheBookIsLaidOut: English part first (translator's preface pp. i-xxi, author's preface, English text pp. 3-54), then the Arabic part, paginated 1-136 from the back of the volume (Hammer: "page 4 of the Arabic text beginning from the right"). The letter tables are printed in the Arabic part and cited in Hammer's English as "v. orig. p." The English part reprints only the four hieroglyph series (English pp. 17-40), the Hermesian letter table (pp. 43-46) and the inline sign groups (pp. 48-49). In a left-to-right scan the Arabic pages run backwards: Arabic page p = leaf 223 - p.

countBreakdown.hammerSays: Translator's preface p. iv: "the eighty alphabets herein deciphered"; p. xii: "the four tables of hieroglyphics". 82 letter tables are printed; counting the Indian "three different sorts" (pp. 6-8) as one alphabet gives 80. Whether Hammer counted so is not stated.

method: Every page in the scan was viewed; table pages were read at 680-1800 px width, the chosen ones at full resolution. Sign counts were made by eye and are exact for the letter tables unless marked; hieroglyph counts are approximate. Arabic headings are transcribed as printed (no added hamzas or dots; "ي" for final ى as in the type); "…" marks words not transcribed.
